plan.contextChunk: This figure is a three-dimensional plot of a single space curve rendered in dark blue against labeled coordinate axes. The vertical z-axis is graduated with ticks and numerals at 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, and 12. The x-axis runs toward the lower left with ticks labeled 2 and 4 in front and -2 and -4 behind, and the y-axis runs toward the lower right with the same labeling, 2 and 4 on the near side and -2 and -4 on the far side. The curve spirals counterclockwise around the vertical axis while climbing steadily, completing roughly two full turns between the xy-plane and the top of the frame above z = 12; its circular cross-section has radius 4, so each loop sweeps out past the ticks marked 4 on both horizontal axes. Two arrowheads placed on the ascending curve show the direction of travel. Across the upper right, in bold, the formula r(t) = 4cost i + 4sint j + t k is printed. Holding the loop radius constant while the height grows in step with the parameter is precisely what produces the spring-like shape. The plot displays the graph of a vector-valued function whose circular motion in the horizontal plane combines with uniform vertical rise to trace a helix.

elements: vertical z-axis drawn as an upward arrow through the origin, with tick marks and numerals 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12

x-axis drawn as a line receding to the lower-left with an arrowhead, ticks labeled 4 and 2 on the near (lower-left) side and -2, -4 on the far (upper-right) side, bold italic label 'x' at the lower-left arrow tip

y-axis drawn as a line receding to the lower-right with an arrowhead, ticks labeled 2 and 4 on the near (lower-right) side and -2, -4 on the far (upper-left) side, bold italic label 'y' at the lower-right arrow tip
dark blue helix of radius 4 spiraling counterclockwise (viewed from +z) and rising from z=0 to just above z=12, about two full turns
two arrowheads on the ascending curve indicating direction of travel: one on the lower loop near y>0 around z~1, one on the upper loop near y>0 around z~6
bold equation label 'r(t) = 4cos t i + 4sin t j + t k' placed in the upper-right of the frame
moving point (marker) on the curve at the current parameter t
faint radial guide segment from the z-axis to the moving point and a vertical dashed drop line from the point to the xy-plane (shows the constant radius 4 and the height z = t)
live readout of t, x = 4cos t, y = 4sin t, z = t

interactions.teaches: The helix is generated by two simultaneous motions: the point circles the z-axis at constant radius while rising at constant rate, so the trail left behind is a spring-like curve.
interactions.label: Trace r(t)

interactions.teaches: Each value of t maps to a single position vector; scrubbing t shows x and y oscillating as cosine and sine while z grows linearly.
interactions.label: t

interactions.teaches: From directly above, the helix collapses onto a single circle of radius 4 — proving the horizontal motion is pure circular motion and all the variation in the 3D shape comes from the rising z = t component.
interactions.label: View

interactions.teaches: Changing the component functions reshapes the space curve, showing that the curve's geometry is entirely determined by the three scalar components of the vector-valued function.

interactions.teaches: Rotating the axonometric view confirms the loops all share the same radius and are stacked in z rather than spiraling inward.

demo_steps.title: The curve and its axes
demo_steps.narration: A single dark-blue space curve winds twice around the vertical z-axis, reaching just past z = 12. The x-axis recedes to the lower left, the y-axis to the lower right.

demo_steps.title: One quarter turn
demo_steps.narration: At t = π/2 the point sits at (0, 4, π/2): x has dropped to 0, y has risen to its maximum 4, and the height equals t.

demo_steps.title: One full loop, height 2π
demo_steps.narration: After t = 2π the point is back over its starting direction (4, 0) but has climbed to z = 2π ≈ 6.28 — the horizontal motion repeats, the vertical motion does not.

demo_steps.title: Look straight down
demo_steps.narration: From above, both loops land on the same circle of radius 4: the horizontal motion is exactly 4cos t i + 4sin t j.

demo_steps.title: Play the motion
demo_steps.narration: Back in 3D, let the point run: constant circling plus constant rise traces the full helix to just above z = 12.

interactionPlan.geometry_notes: World units equal graph units. Helix: x=4cos t, y=4sin t, z=t for t in [0, 12.8] (about 2.04 turns), radius exactly 4, top just above z=12. Axes: z-axis from z=-0.5 to z=13.5 (arrow at top, ticks/numerals at 2,4,6,8,10,12 on the left side of the axis); x-axis spans -5 to 5 along the screen-lower-left/upper-right diagonal with the POSITIVE end toward the lower left (label 'x' there, ticks 2 and 4 on that near side, -2 and -4 on the far upper-right side); y-axis spans -5 to 5 along the screen-lower-right/upper-left diagonal with the POSITIVE end toward the lower right (label 'y' there, ticks 2 and 4 near, -2 and -4 far). Tick marks are short strokes drawn perpendicular to each horizontal axis in the xy-plane. Origin at world (0,0,0), placed roughly at the lower-third center of the frame so the helix occupies the upper two-thirds. Curve color dark navy-blue #1F4E79 / #16537e, line width ~2.5 px; axes and tick labels black, thin (~1 px); equation text black bold, upper right. Direction arrowheads tangent to the curve at t≈1.2 (z≈1.2, near the front-right of the lowest loop) and t≈6.0 (z≈6.0, front-right of the second loop), both pointing in the direction of increasing t (counterclockwise seen from +z, i.e. up-and-to-the-right on screen). Moving point: filled sphere/disc radius ~0.25, orange-red #c0392b for contrast. Radial guide segment from (0,0,z) to the point, and dashed vertical line from the point down to (x,y,0), both light gray ~40% opacity.
interactionPlan.notes: Use an OrthographicCamera for the axonometric look (standard isometric pose, no perspective convergence). Build the helix with THREE.Line from a sampled parametric curve (≥600 points) so the animated trail can be drawn by setting drawRange from 0 to the current t index — the untraced remainder can be shown faintly or hidden during the animation. Axis arrowheads as small ConeGeometry; tick numerals and 'x'/'y'/'z' labels and the bold equation as CSS2DObject/HTML overlays so they stay screen-aligned and crisp. For the top-view toggle, animate the camera to look straight down -z (elevation 90°) over ~0.6 s and fade the z-axis ticks; the helix then reads as a circle of radius 4. Equation input: parse x(t), y(t), z(t) at runtime with a small safe expression evaluator (sin, cos, tan, exp, log, sqrt, pow, pi, e), resample 600 points over t in [0, 12.8], rebuild the line geometry, and auto-fit/clamp the axis extents; on a parse error keep the last valid curve and show the message inline beneath the offending field. Slider and animation share the same t state so scrubbing pauses playback.

plan.authoredInteractions:
- Animation for tracing r(t): the learner plays the motion, a point moves around the circle while rising at constant speed and leaves the helix behind, making the combination of circular horizontal motion and linear vertical motion visible.
- Slider for parameter t: the learner scrubs t, the point advances along the helix with live x=4cos(t), y=4sin(t), and z=t values, showing how the vector-valued function maps time to position.
- Toggle between top view and 3D view: the learner switches views, the helix collapses to a radius-4 circle from above and returns to a rising spiral in 3D, clarifying that constant radius and increasing height together form the helix.
- Equation input for the parametric curve: learner edits x(t), y(t), and z(t), pre-filled with 4*cos(t), 4*sin(t), and t; the helix redraws and the moving point follows the new curve over the same t interval.

authoredContext:
As mentioned, the name of the shape of the curve of the graph in the examplec. is a helix (the figure). The curve resembles a spring, with a circular cross-section looking down along the z-axis. It is possible for a helix to be elliptical in cross-section as well. For example, the vector-valued function r(t)=4costi+3sintj+tk describes an elliptical helix. The projection of this helix into the x,y-plane is an ellipse. Last, the arrows in the graph of this helix indicate the orientation of the curve as t progresses from 0 to 4π.

The graph of the third vector-valued function is a helix.

This figure is the graph of a helix in the 3 dimensional coordinate system. The curve represents the function r(t) = cost i + sint j + tk. The curve spirals in a circular path around the vertical z-axis and has the look of a spring. The arrows on the curve represent orientation.

discrepancies: Numeric tick labels (2,4,6,8,10,12 on z; ±2,±4 on x and y), the axis letters x/y/z, and the r(t) = 4cos t i + 4sin t j + t k equation caption are not discernible in the render — the source figure's most prominent text (the equation at top right and the scale numbers) does not read at all at the current size/placement.
Extra elements not in the source: a red position marker sphere plus grey radial and dashed drop lines are always shown, so the default view is not a clean match for the textbook figure.

The z-axis in the source rises well above the top of the helix (to ~13 with a clear arrow and numbered ticks); in the render the axis arrow is barely above the top loop, making the vertical scale look compressed relative to the loop radius.
The figure is drawn quite small within the canvas (large empty margin on the left), whereas the source fills its frame; combined with tiny labels this hurts readability.
evaluation.notes: The helix, axis triad with ticks, navy curve colour, and direction arrowheads reproduce the source composition well and the interaction set (t slider, trace playback, top-view toggle, editable component functions, guided steps) is rich and conceptually apt — but the annotation layer (axis numerals, x/y/z letters, and especially the r(t) equation) is effectively invisible at the rendered scale, and added marker/guide lines depart from the clean textbook look.
action_items: Increase label font sizes (axis numerals ~13-14px, axis letters bold 15px, equation caption 16px bold with a light background) and verify they render visibly; place the equation caption at the top-right as in the source.
Extend the z-axis clearly above the top of the helix and enlarge the overall scene framing (raise heightFraction / reduce margin) so the figure fills the canvas like the source.
Hide the red marker, radial line and dashed drop line at t = 0 / step 1 so the default state matches the textbook figure, revealing them only once the slider or trace is used.
Ensure both on-curve direction arrowheads are positioned at the same heights as the source (~z≈1.5 and z≈6) and are clearly visible against the curve.

interactionPlan.geometry_notes: World units equal graph units. Helix: x=4cos t, y=4sin t, z=t for t in [0, 12.8] (about 2.04 turns), radius exactly 4, top just above z=12. Axes: z-axis from z=-0.5 to z=13.5 (arrow at top, ticks/numerals at 2,4,6,8,10,12 on the left side of the axis); x-axis spans -5 to 5 along the screen-lower-left/upper-right diagonal with the POSITIVE end toward the lower left (label 'x' there, ticks 2 and 4 on that near side, -2 and -4 on the far upper-right side); y-axis spans -5 to 5 along the screen-lower-right/upper-left diagonal with the POSITIVE end toward the lower right (label 'y' there, ticks 2 and 4 near, -2 and -4 far). Tick marks are short strokes drawn perpendicular to each horizontal axis in the xy-plane. Origin at world (0,0,0), placed roughly at the lower-third center of the frame so the helix occupies the upper two-thirds. Curve color dark navy-blue #1F4E79 / #16537e, line width ~2.5 px; axes and tick labels black, thin (~1 px); equation text black bold, upper right. Direction arrowheads tangent to the curve at t≈1.2 (z≈1.2, near the front-right of the lowest loop) and t≈6.0 (z≈6.0, front-right of the second loop), both pointing in the direction of increasing t (counterclockwise seen from +z, i.e. up-and-to-the-right on screen). Moving point: filled sphere/disc radius ~0.25, orange-red #c0392b for contrast. Radial guide segment from (0,0,z) to the point, and dashed vertical line from the point down to (x,y,0), both light gray ~40% opacity.
interactionPlan.notes: Use an OrthographicCamera for the axonometric look (standard isometric pose, no perspective convergence). Build the helix with THREE.Line from a sampled parametric curve (≥600 points) so the animated trail can be drawn by setting drawRange from 0 to the current t index — the untraced remainder can be shown faintly or hidden during the animation. Axis arrowheads as small ConeGeometry; tick numerals and 'x'/'y'/'z' labels and the bold equation as CSS2DObject/HTML overlays so they stay screen-aligned and crisp. For the top-view toggle, animate the camera to look straight down -z (elevation 90°) over ~0.6 s and fade the z-axis ticks; the helix then reads as a circle of radius 4. Equation input: parse x(t), y(t), z(t) at runtime with a small safe expression evaluator (sin, cos, tan, exp, log, sqrt, pow, pi, e), resample 600 points over t in [0, 12.8], rebuild the line geometry, and auto-fit/clamp the axis extents; on a parse error keep the last valid curve and show the message inline beneath the offending field. Slider and animation share the same t state so scrubbing pauses playback.

plan.authoredPrompt: This figure is a three-dimensional plot of a single space curve rendered in dark blue against labeled coordinate axes. The vertical z-axis is graduated with ticks and numerals at 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, and 12. The x-axis runs toward the lower left with ticks labeled 2 and 4 in front and -2 and -4 behind, and the y-axis runs toward the lower right with the same labeling, 2 and 4 on the near side and -2 and -4 on the far side. The curve spirals counterclockwise around the vertical axis while climbing steadily, completing roughly two full turns between the xy-plane and the top of the frame above z = 12; its circular cross-section has radius 4, so each loop sweeps out past the ticks marked 4 on both horizontal axes. Two arrowheads placed on the ascending curve show the direction of travel. Across the upper right, in bold, the formula r(t) = 4cost i + 4sint j + t k is printed. Holding the loop radius constant while the height grows in step with the parameter is precisely what produces the spring-like shape. The plot displays the graph of a vector-valued function whose circular motion in the horizontal plane combines with uniform vertical rise to trace a helix.
plan.authoredInteractions:
- Animation for tracing r(t): the learner plays the motion, a point moves around the circle while rising at constant speed and leaves the helix behind, making the combination of circular horizontal motion and linear vertical motion visible.
- Slider for parameter t: the learner scrubs t, the point advances along the helix with live x=4cos(t), y=4sin(t), and z=t values, showing how the vector-valued function maps time to position.
- Toggle between top view and 3D view: the learner switches views, the helix collapses to a radius-4 circle from above and returns to a rising spiral in 3D, clarifying that constant radius and increasing height together form the helix.
- Equation input for the parametric curve: learner edits x(t), y(t), and z(t), pre-filled with 4*cos(t), 4*sin(t), and t; the helix redraws and the moving point follows the new curve over the same t interval.

discrepancies: The second direction arrowhead (t ≈ 6) renders as a small filled blob on the left side of the middle loop instead of the clean, clearly-oriented arrowhead the source places on the upper-right portion of the curve at z ≈ 6; only the lower arrowhead reads correctly as a direction marker.

The z-axis in the generated figure extends noticeably above the 12 tick with a long bare shaft and arrow, whereas in the source the axis terminates shortly above 12, slightly changing the vertical proportions of the composition.
Tick-mark styling differs: the source draws multiple closely-spaced hash marks along the x and y axes between the labelled values, while the generated figure shows only single ticks at ±2 and ±4.
evaluation.notes: A faithful, well-composed 3D reproduction of the textbook helix with correct isometric axis orientation, navy curve, tick labels and equation, backed by genuinely useful interactions (t slider, trace animation, top-view toggle, editable component functions, guided steps); only small issues remain with one direction arrowhead's appearance/placement and minor axis proportion/tick-style differences.
action_items: Reposition/reorient the second tangent arrowhead so it sits on the upper-right ascending segment near z ≈ 6 as in the source and reads clearly as a cone rather than a dot from the default camera.
Shorten the z-axis so it terminates just above the z = 12 tick, matching the source's vertical framing.
Add the finer intermediate hash marks along the x- and y-axes (as in the source) so the ticks between −4 and 4 look like the original ruled axes.
Consider a faint grey drop-circle or shadow in the xy-plane only when the marker is revealed, so the default view stays identical to the source.
